column1: # THE BILL OF MATERIALS FOR A JAVA 11 BUMP. Hand maintained, on purpose.
# Floors.java states these same facts as prose, because that is what a planner reads and a planner
# reads prose better than a table. This is the other half of the same fact, in the shape a program
# can act on, and it is written by hand rather than parsed out of the prose: a parser over those
# lines is exactly what once decided every floor was met and skipped the phase for a whole corpus.
# Two hand-written lists drift instead, which is a different risk and a louder one -- a test walks
# both and fails the build the moment a coordinate or a version disagrees.
# Today this is measured against. It is meant to become the thing a deterministic pinning step
# applies, at which point the prose stops carrying versions at all.
#   group:artifact   the canonical name, as Floors writes it
#   phase            before | after -- which side of the JDK change it can be raised on
#   dialect          any | maven | gradle -- which build systems can express it at all. A row a
#                    build system cannot have does not count against it; counting an impossible
#                    row as a miss turns a percentage into an accusation.
#   spellings        every other name a build file may use for this same artifact, comma separated.
#                    Without these the measurement is a lie on half the corpus: Gradle cannot write
